title: Sample, Mix, or Verify? Allocating Test-Time Compute under Imperfect Verifiers
abstract: arXiv:2610.23255v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: A common way to make language models and agents more accurate is to spend more compute at inference time: generate many candidate solutions and submit the one a verifier prefers. Success then requires that some candidate is correct and that the verifier picks it. The first grows predictably with the number of samples; the second does not, because real verifiers (unit tests, majority votes, LLM judges, reward models) accept wrong answers, reject right ones, and make correlated mistakes. With a fixed budget, a practitioner must decide how many samples to draw, which models to draw them from, and how much to spend on verification, and today these choices are made by rules of thumb. We introduce SPLIT, which makes them from a small labelled pilot. translated_title: 采样、混合还是验证？不完美验证器下的测试时计算分配
translated_abstract: arXiv:2610.23255v1 公告类型：cross 摘要：让语言模型和智能体更准确的一种常见方法是在推理阶段投入更多计算：生成大量候选解决方案，并提交验证器所偏好的那一个。成功需要满足两个条件：存在正确的候选解，且验证器能将其选出。前者随样本数量的增加而可预测地提升；后者却并非如此，因为真实的验证器（单元测试、多数投票、LLM 裁判、奖励模型）会接受错误答案、拒绝正确答案，并且会犯具有相关性的错误。在预算固定的情况下，从业者必须决定抽取多少样本、从哪些模型中抽取，以及在验证上投入多少资源，而目前这些选择都是凭经验法则做出的。我们提出 SPLIT，它基于一个小的带标签试点实验来做出这些决策。其核心是一个精确公式，用于计算在接受/拒绝和最高分选择机制下提交正确答案的概率，该公式考虑了任务难度的变化以及各模型之间共享的盲点……
tldr: 该论文提出 SPLIT 方法，利用小型带标签试点实验和精确概率公式，在验证器不完美的情况下科学地分配测试时计算预算（采样数量、模型选择与验证开销）。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces SPLIT, which leverages a small labelled pilot and an exact probability formula to optimally allocate test-time compute—sample counts, model choices, and verification spend—under imperfect verifiers.
